items.title: Tanzania celebrates first natural gas discovery in more than 10 years
items.summary: The energy minister described it as a "major milestone" for the East African nation Tanzania has announced a significant discovery of natural gas in the Mnazi Bay area in the south of the country - the first such find in a decade Energy Minister Juma Homera attended a ceremony at the Kasa-1X ST2 well, which is jointly owned by state-owned Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation (TPDC) and French oil firm Maurel & Prom, to mark the occasion He said the estimated 223 billion cubic feet (6.3 billion cubic metres) discovery was a "major milestone" in the development of the small oil and gas sector in the East African nation The new well is expected to start production early next month and is intended to boost domestic supplies Tanzania has existing natural gas reserves of 57.54 trillion cubic feet Gas from the field will be for domestic and industrial power generation and also for vehicles "The discovery is important in ensuring the country has reliable, clean and safe energy at affordable costs, particularly at a time when demand is increasing due to industrial growth and other…

items.title: Mozambique: Helios to acquire 49% stake in Merec Industries
items.summary: Helios Fund V will acquire the stake in Merec, described as Mozambique’s largest flour milling company. According to the companies, the transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions including regulatory approvals, after which Invictus Investment will remain the majority shareholder Founded in 1998, Merec processes wheat and corn into an integrated portfolio spanning flour, pasta, biscuits and animal feed. Its mills, production facilities and silos are located in each of Mozambique’s three principal port regions – Beira, Maputo and Nacala – making it the only miller with manufacturing facilities in all three. Merec also owns a grain terminal at the port of Maputo, and its footprint supports a nationwide distribution network serving wholesalers, retailers, bakeries, feed producers and distributors Invictus Investment acquired Merec in January 2025 through the purchase of Stratton Africa Holdings.

items.title: Judoka determined to prove refugees belong at Dakar 2026
items.summary: Arno Yafunga Botay is one of six athletes competing for the Refugee Olympic Team at the Dakar 2026 Youth Games Arno Yafunga Botay was six when his family fled the Democratic Republic of Congo after threats to his father's life culminated in an attack on their home which claimed the life of his seven-month-old sibling Following a spell living in the Kakuma refugee camp in north-west Kenya, the family settled in Nairobi. There, Arno used to watch his father Arnold practising judo and eventually asked him to teach him the sport Now, having coming through trials in East Africa , he will compete for the Refugee Olympic Team in the under-55kg category at the Dakar 2026 Youth Games "I didn't expect to be selected," the 15-year-old told BBC Sport Africa "I was so excited.

items.title: Mozambique’s only radiotherapy machine remains out of service – minister
items.summary: “We have the only radiotherapy machine in the country here, and it is out of service. During this term of government, we have tried to rehabilitate this equipment,” Health Minister Ussene Isse said at the opening of the second edition of the Mozambique Medical Expo in Maputo, a platform bringing together public and private institutions, companies and healthcare professionals to discuss opportunities and challenges in the sector “Radiotherapy is a key weapon in treating some cancers; it saves lives. So you can imagine the pain we carry every day as we try to get that machine working again. This is a challenge because the machine’s parts are no longer available on the market; they have been discontinued,” he said Radiotherapy is one of the main treatments used to combat cancer, and the unavailability of the equipment forces Mozambican patients to seek treatment abroad, at considerable cost to families and the State “We cannot lose Mozambicans; we have to send people abroad for radiotherapy.

items.title: Mozambique signs agreement with China to restructure its debt
items.summary: Maputo, 28 Oct (AIM) – Mozambique’s public debt with China will be restructured following the signing of a Supplementary Framework Agreement between the governments’ of both countries. The agreement follows meetings held in China last April between Mozambican President Daniel Chapo and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, in which China granted a partial forgiveness of Mozambique’s debt, amounting to 204 million yuan (1.9 billion meticais) in interest-free loans that were set to mature in December 2024. The agreement was signed by the finance minister Carla Louveira and the Chinese ambassador to Mozambique Zheng Xuan. The agreement aligns with the Medium-Term Public Debt Management Strategy (2025–2029) and represents a significant step toward aligning debt repayments with the country’s financial capacity, thereby strengthening the sustainability of public finances.

items.title: Flavio Bolsonaro lands in US, declares himself 'leader' of Brazil
items.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro declared himself the rightful leader of his country despite losing the presidential election runoff on Sunday. He and his family have fled to the US Brazilian right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro declared himself the rightful leader of Brazil after landing in Miami with his family on Wednesday Bolsonaro fled Brazil after the Supreme Court asked him to hand over his passports so he couldn't leave the country The right-wing senator had not conceded defeat in Sunday's presidential election to rival, President Luiz Inacio "Lula"da Silva Bolsonaro lost elections on Sunday and alleged irregularities. His party has acknowledged the results of Sunday's elections and international observers have observed it was fair.

items.title: Israel's election deadlock is a sign of the country's deep divisions
items.summary: "Democracy is the worst form of government except for all those other forms that have been tried." So said Winston Churchill in the House of Commons in 1947 His aphorism came to mind as Israel's election results filtered through on Tuesday night - exit polls blending with ballots that were cast to dash or fulfil people's hopes and fears This election has, in some ways, been a celebration of democracy. Voters turning out in record numbers, Jews and Arabs alike. Many spent thousands to fly in from abroad to cast their ballot At polling stations across the country, we saw the passion of campaigners, as they used every minute to try to change that last mind and win that last vote President Isaac Herzog said the election was a "badge of honour" for Israeli society. "It is remarkable to see how deep the desire for democracy is in Israel," he exclaimed Yet this election left the most established democracy in the Middle East without a clear path to a new government.
